text: Soon whispers about the lovers spread among the people and enemies began to watch them, until at last Arsats brother told him that he must take the woman away. <break time="0.8s" /> The chance came on a night when the Ruler and all his people went down to the mouth of the river to catch fish by the light of countless torches. <break time="0.8s" /> While the crowd was busy with the fishing, the brothers slipped away in a small canoe, and Diamelen came running toward them along the dark shore. <break time="0.8s" /> Arsat lifted her into the canoe, and the brothers paddled with all their strength down the river and out to the open sea, hardly speaking a word all night. <break time="0.8s" /> When the sun rose, they were moving along the coast, and Arsats brother would not let them rest, for he knew that the Rulers men would soon be after them. <break time="0.8s" /> Not until the sun was high did Arsat, exhausted, beg for a short rest, and his brother at last agreed to stop in a bay of white sand near a cape. <break time="0.8s" /> Diamelen had hardly fallen asleep on the sand when she woke with a cry, for a boat of the Rulers men was coming toward the bay, its gong sounding across the water. <break time="0.8s" /> Arsats brother carried a gun that the white man had once given him, though he had only a handful of powder, and he quickly made a plan to save the others. <break time="0.8s" /> Run through the forest to the fishermans hut on the other side, he said, and take his canoe, while I hold them back here, and then I will follow you.
